name: BURUNDI

flag.title: Flag of Burundi
flag.note: Red & green split by white saltire + 3 stars

lead: Burundi is a small country in East Africa with no coast. Green ridges drop to Lake Tanganyika, one of the world's deepest lakes. Its cool highlands earned it the name "Switzerland of Africa." People here love royal drums and running.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Burundi sits on high, flat land averaging 1,500 m above sea level, so the air feels cool and breezy. Forested ridges ripple east to west. Banana plants crowd the valley slopes.
Lake Tanganyika runs along the whole west edge. It is 676 km long and 1,471 m deep. Some of its fish live nowhere else on Earth.
animals: Kibira National Park in the northwest is Burundi's wildest corner. Its 400 km² of rainforest echo with chimpanzee calls at dawn. Colobus monkeys leap through the treetops.
Hippos wallow where the Rusizi River meets the lake. Under Lake Tanganyika, over 130 species of cichlid fish shimmer in bright colours.
culture: The ingoma drum is the heartbeat of Burundi. Royal drummers in red, white, and green beat huge drums while dancing. UNESCO listed this tradition in 2014.
Most families farm plantains, sweet potatoes, and sorghum on hillsides. Friends share urwagwa, a lightly fizzy banana beer, from one pot through long straws.
history: For centuries, Burundi was a strong kingdom. A new mwami (king) was said to 'ascend the drum'. Belgium took control after World War I.
Burundi became independent on 1 July 1962. Civil conflict followed, but a peace deal in 2000 rebuilt calm. Today a young population is shaping a new future.
wows: Burundi's flag has a rare diagonal cross, a saltire, dividing red and green fields.
A spring on Mount Gikizi in southern Burundi is the River Nile's most distant source.
Vénuste Niyongabo won Burundi's first Olympic gold in 1996, in the 5,000 m race.
Lake Tanganyika holds 17% of Earth's unfrozen fresh surface water and is its second deepest lake.
Burundi is Africa's third most crowded country, twice as crowded per km² as France.
Scientists found the Bururi long-fingered frog in 2011, after thinking it extinct since 1949.
Gishora Sanctuary has two sacred drums nobody has ever struck.

myths.myth: Burundi and Rwanda are one country
myths.fact: They are two countries, each with its own government, capital, and flag.
Hippos cannot swim. They are too heavy to float, so they walk along riverbeds.
